translations.idiomatic: His fame rushed to Luoyang; every scholar-official yearned to meet him.

sentences.zh: 后乃驾驴车，与诸生俱诣许下。

translations.literal: Later he then drove a donkey cart and together with several students went to Xu below.
translations.idiomatic: He later hitched a donkey cart and rode to the capital with a train of pupils.

sentences.zh: 道过荥阳，止主人舍，而所驾之驴忽然卒僵，蛆虫流出，主遽白之。

translations.literal: Passing through Xingyang he stopped at his host's inn, and the donkey he was driving suddenly died stiff, maggots flowing out; the host hurriedly informed him.
translations.idiomatic: At an Xingyang inn his donkey dropped dead, maggots pouring from its hide; the innkeeper panicked.

sentences.zh: 子训曰：“乃尔乎？

translations.literal: Zixun said, "Is it thus?
translations.idiomatic: Zixun murmured, "So soon?

sentences.zh: ”方安坐饭，食毕，徐出以杖扣之，驴应声奋起，行步如初，即复进道。

translations.literal: " He then sat calmly eating; when the meal was finished he slowly went out and tapped it with his staff; the donkey responded to the sound and leaped up, walking as at first, and immediately proceeded on the road again.
translations.idiomatic: " He finished dinner in calm, tapped the carcass with his staff, and the beast sprang up sound as ever.

sentences.zh: 其追逐观者常有千数。

translations.literal: Those who chased to watch were often a thousand or more in number.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds in the thousands chased his cart.

sentences.zh: 既到京师，公卿以下候之者，坐上恒数百人，皆为设酒脯，终日不匮。

translations.literal: When he had reached the capital, from ministers of state downward those who waited for him—several hundred people constantly sat in his hall—he all set out wine and dried meat for them, and all day it was not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang hundreds packed his hall; he fed them wine and meat all day without running dry.

sentences.zh: 后因遁去，遂不知所止。

translations.literal: Later because he slipped away, no one knew where he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Then he vanished, and none could trace him.

sentences.zh: 初去之日，唯见白云腾起，从旦至暮，如是数十处。

translations.literal: On the day he first left, people only saw white clouds rise up, from dawn to dusk thus at several tens of places.
translations.idiomatic: The day he left, white pillars of cloud rose in dozens of places from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 时有百岁翁，自说童兒时见子训卖药于会稽市，颜色不异于今。

translations.literal: At that time there was a hundred-year-old man who himself said that in his childhood he had seen Zixun selling medicine in the market of Kuaiji, his complexion no different from now.
translations.idiomatic: A centenarian swore he had bought Zixun's physic in Kuaiji as a boy—the man's face had not aged.

sentences.zh: 后人复于长安东霸城见之，与一老公共摩挲铜人，相谓曰：“适见铸此，已近五百岁矣。

translations.literal: Later people again saw him east of Chang'an at Bawang City, rubbing a bronze man together with an old man, saying to each other, "Just now we saw this cast; it is already nearly five hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Later witnesses saw him east of Chang'an at Bawang, polishing a bronze statue with a greybeard, murmuring, "We watched them cast this—nearly five hundred years ago.

sentences.zh: ”顾视见人而去，犹驾昔所乘驴车也。

translations.literal: " They looked around, saw people, and departed, still driving the same donkey cart they had formerly ridden.
translations.idiomatic: " Spotting onlookers, they drove off in the same donkey cart as before.

sentences.zh: 见者呼之曰：“蓟先生小住。

translations.literal: Those who saw them called to them, saying, "Master Ji, pause a little.
translations.idiomatic: "Wait, Master Ji!" a bystander cried.

sentences.zh: ”并行应之，视若迟徐，而走马不及，于是而绝。

translations.literal: " Walking in parallel they answered him; he looked as if he were slow, yet a galloping horse could not overtake him, and thus he was lost to sight.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered while ambling, yet no horse could close the gap—and then they were gone.

sentences.zh: 刘根者，颍川人也。

translations.literal: Liu Gen was a man of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gen hailed from Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 隐居嵩山中。

translations.literal: He concealed himself and lived in Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: He hid himself on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 诸好事者，自远而至，就根学道，太守史祈以根为妖妄，乃收执诣郡，数之曰：“汝有何术，而诬惑百姓？

translations.literal: Various persons fond of such matters came from afar to study the Way with Gen; Grand Administrator Shi Qi thought Gen was deceitful and wild, and therefore arrested and seized him, brought him to the commandery, and reckoned with him, saying, "What arts do you have, that you delude and confuse the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Curious seekers trekked to study under him; Prefect Shi Qi branded him a charlatan, hauled him in, and demanded, "What trick lets you beguile the people?

sentences.zh: 若果有神，可显一验事。

translations.literal: If you truly have spirits, you can display one verification.
translations.idiomatic: If spirits truly attend you, prove it once.

sentences.zh: 不尔，立死矣。

translations.literal: If not so, you will immediately die.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you die on the spot.

sentences.zh: ”根曰：“实无它异，颇能令人见鬼耳。

translations.literal: " Gen said, "In truth I have no other strangeness; I am only rather able to make people see ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Gen said, "I have no marvel except this—I can make you see ghosts.

sentences.zh: ”祈曰：“促召之，使太守目睹，尔乃为明。

translations.literal: " Qi said, "Hasten to summon them; make the grand administrator witness with his own eyes, and only then is it clear.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Qi barked, "Call them now—let this prefect see with his own eyes.

sentences.zh: ”根于是左顾而啸，有顷，祈之亡父祖近亲数十人，皆反缚在前，向根叩头曰：“小兒无状，分当万坐。

translations.literal: " Gen therefore looked left and whistled; after a moment, several tens of Qi's deceased fathers, grandfathers, and close kin, all with arms bound behind, were in front, and toward Gen knocked their heads, saying, "The boy has no manners; by rights he deserves death ten thousand times.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Gen glanced left and whistled; scores of Shi's dead kin appeared bound, kowtowed to Gen, and cried, "Our descendant is worthless—he deserves death a thousandfold.

sentences.zh: ”顾而叱祈曰：“汝为子孙，不能有益先人，而反累辱亡灵！

translations.literal: " They looked back and berated Qi, saying, "You as descendant cannot benefit your forebears, yet instead repeatedly shame the spirits of the dead!
translations.idiomatic: " They wheeled on Shi Qi: "You honor no ancestor yet heap shame on our shades!

sentences.zh: 可叩头为吾陈谢。

translations.literal: Knock your head and on our behalf present an apology.
translations.idiomatic: Kowtow and beg his pardon on our behalf.

sentences.zh: ”祈惊惧悲哀，顿首流血，请自甘罪坐。

translations.literal: " Qi was alarmed, afraid, and grieved; he knocked his head until blood flowed and begged to accept guilt and punishment himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qi blanched, beat his brow bloody, and begged to suffer in their stead.

sentences.zh: 根嘿而不应，忽然俱去，不知在所。

translations.literal: Gen was silent and did not answer; suddenly they all departed, and no one knew where they were.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gen sat silent; the phantoms vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 左慈字元放，庐江人也。

translations.literal: Zuo Ci, courtesy name Yuanfang, was a man of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Ci, styled Yuanfang, came from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 少有神道。

translations.literal: In his youth he had the way of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he commanded uncanny arts.

sentences.zh: 尝在司空曹操坐，操从容顾众宾曰：“今日高会，珍羞略备，所少吴松江鲈鱼耳。

translations.literal: He once sat in Minister of Works Cao Cao's company; Cao Cao leisurely looked around at the assembled guests and said, "Today's lofty gathering, rare delicacies are in general prepared; what is lacking is only the perch of the Wu-Song River.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet hosted by Minister Cao Cao, Cao surveyed his guests and said, "We have every delicacy—only the perch of the Wu-Song is missing.

sentences.zh: ”放于下坐应曰：“此可得也。

translations.literal: " Ci from the lower seats replied, saying, "This can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: " From the lower seats Zuo Ci answered, "That can be arranged.

sentences.zh: ”因求铜盘贮水，以竹竿饵钓于盘中，须臾引一鲈鱼出。

translations.literal: " Therefore he sought a bronze basin to store water, baited a hook with a bamboo pole in the basin, and in a moment drew out one perch.
translations.idiomatic: " He asked for a copper pan of water, baited a bamboo rod in it, and in moments hauled up a Song perch.

sentences.zh: 操大拊掌笑，会者皆惊。

translations.literal: Cao Cao greatly clapped his hands and laughed; all who attended were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Cao roared with laughter and slapped his thighs; every guest gaped.

sentences.zh: 操曰：“一鱼不周坐席，可更得乎？

translations.literal: Cao Cao said, "One fish does not suffice for the seats; can you get more?
translations.idiomatic: Cao said, "One fish will not feed the table—can you fetch more?

sentences.zh: ”放乃更饵钩沉之，须臾复引出，皆长三尺余，生鲜可爱。

translations.literal: " Fang then again baited his hook and sank it; in a moment he again drew them out; all were more than three chi in length, fresh and lovely to look at.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuo baited again, dipped the line, and pulled up more perch, each over three feet long, gleaming and firm.

sentences.zh: 操使目前□会之，周浃会者。

translations.literal: Cao Cao had them sliced before his eyes for the assembly, so that it circulated to all who attended.
translations.idiomatic: Cao had the fish sliced on the spot and passed the platters until every guest was served.

sentences.zh: 操又谓曰：“既已得鱼，恨无蜀中生姜耳。

translations.literal: Cao Cao again said to him, "Since we have already obtained fish, I regret that we lack ginger from Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao added, "We have the fish, but no Sichuan ginger to season it.

sentences.zh: ”放曰：“亦可得也。

translations.literal: " Fang said, "That too can be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuo said, "Ginger can be had as well.

sentences.zh: ”操恐其近即所取，因曰：“吾前遣人到蜀买锦，可过敕使者，增市二端。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao feared he would fetch it from nearby on the spot, and therefore said, "Earlier I sent someone to Shu to buy brocade; you may pass by and instruct the envoy to add two bolts to the purchase.
translations.idiomatic: " Fearing he would conjure the root from thin air, Cao said, "I lately sent a man to Shu for brocade—tell that envoy to add two extra bolts to his order.

sentences.zh: ”语顷，即得姜还，并获操使报命。

translations.literal: " In the space of speaking he obtained ginger and returned, and also captured Cao Cao's messenger reporting completion of the mission.
translations.idiomatic: " A moment later he produced the ginger along with Cao's courier, clutching the receipt.

sentences.zh: 后操使蜀反，验问增锦之状及时日早晚，若符契焉。

translations.literal: Later when Cao Cao's envoy returned from Shu, he verified and asked about the circumstances of the added brocade and the early or late timing of the day; it was as if tally slips matched.
translations.idiomatic: When the real envoy returned from Shu, his report of the extra brocade matched Zuo's tale to the hour.

sentences.zh: 后操出近郊，士大夫从者百许人，慈乃为赍酒一升，脯一斤，手自斟酌，百官莫不醉饱。

translations.literal: Later Cao Cao went out to the near suburbs; more than a hundred gentlemen and great officials followed; Ci then for them brought one sheng of wine and one jin of dried meat, personally pouring for them, and none of the hundred officials failed to be drunk and full.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cao rode to the suburbs with a hundred officials; Zuo produced a pint of wine and a pound of jerky, poured for each man himself, and left every guest drunk and stuffed.

sentences.zh: 操怪之，使寻其故，行视诸垆，悉亡其酒脯矣。

translations.literal: Cao Cao thought it strange and sent men to seek the reason; going about to inspect the various wine-shops, all had lost their wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: Cao sent runners to trace the miracle—every tavern in town was missing the same wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 操怀不喜，因坐上收，欲杀之，慈乃却入壁中，霍然不知所在。

translations.literal: Cao Cao harbored displeasure, and therefore on the seat arrested him, intending to kill him; Ci then drew back into the wall, and in a flash no one knew where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious and angry, Cao ordered his arrest at table; Zuo stepped backward into the plaster and vanished.

sentences.zh: 或见于市者，又捕之，而市人皆变形与慈同，莫知谁是。

translations.literal: When someone saw him in the market they again tried to seize him, but the people of the market all changed form to be identical with Ci, and no one knew which was he.
translations.idiomatic: Spotters cornered him in the market, yet every shopper wore Zuo's face—no one could tell which was real.

sentences.zh: 后人逢慈于阳城山头，因复逐之，遂入走羊群。

translations.literal: Later people encountered Ci on the summit of Yangcheng Mountain; they therefore again pursued him, and he thereupon entered and ran into a flock of sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Later they sighted him on Yangcheng peak; chasing him, they watched him bolt into a flock of sheep.

sentences.zh: 操知不可得，乃令就羊中告之曰：“不复相杀，本试君术耳。

translations.literal: Cao Cao knew he could not be obtained, and therefore ordered someone to go among the sheep and announce to them, saying, "I will not kill you again; originally I was only testing your arts.
translations.idiomatic: Cao saw capture was futile and shouted into the flock, "No more killing—I was only testing your skill.

sentences.zh: ”忽有一老羝屈前两膝，人立而言曰：“遽如许。

translations.literal: " Suddenly one old ram bent its two foreknees, stood like a man, and spoke, saying, "So suddenly like this.
translations.idiomatic: " An old ram rose on its knees like a man and bleated, "Why such haste?".

sentences.zh: ”即竞往赴之，而群羊数百皆变为羝，并屈前膝人立，云“遽如许”，遂莫知所取焉。

translations.literal: " They immediately all rushed to go to it, but several hundred sheep in the flock all changed into rams, all bending their foreknees and standing like humans, saying "So suddenly like this," and therefore none knew which to take.
translations.idiomatic: " The hunters rushed the speaker—only to see hundreds of rams kneel upright, each crying the same phrase, so none could pick the sage.

sentences.zh: 计子勋

translations.literal: Ji Zixun
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zixun

sentences.zh: 计子勋者，不知何郡县人，皆谓数百步，行来于人间。

translations.literal: As for Ji Zixun, no one knew from what commandery or county he was; all said that for several hundred paces he walked back and forth among mankind.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zixun's home county is lost; folk said he paced a few hundred steps at a time as he wandered among them.

sentences.zh: 一旦忽言日中当死，主人与之葛衣，子勋服而正寝，至日中果死。

translations.literal: One morning he suddenly said that at midday he ought to die; his host gave him a kudzu garment, Zixun put it on and lay straight as for sleep, and when midday came he indeed died.
translations.idiomatic: One dawn he announced he would die at noon; his host gave him a hemp robe, he lay down composed—and at noon he was dead.

sentences.zh: 上成公者，密县人也。

translations.literal: Shang Chenggong was a man of Mi county.
translations.idiomatic: The adept Shang Chenggong came from Mi county.

sentences.zh: 其初行久而不还，后归，语其家云：“我已得仙。

translations.literal: At first he walked a long time and did not return; later he returned and said to his family, "I have already obtained immortality.
translations.idiomatic: He once vanished for ages, then returned to tell his kin, "I have become an immortal.

sentences.zh: ”因辞家而去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took leave of his family and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " He bade them farewell and left.

sentences.zh: 家人见其举步稍高，良久乃没云。

translations.literal: The family members saw that each step he took was somewhat higher, and after a long while he then disappeared into the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: They watched each stride lift him higher until he faded into the clouds.

sentences.zh: 陈寔、韩韶同见其事。

translations.literal: Chen Shi and Han Shao together witnessed this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shi and Han Shao both saw it happen.

sentences.zh: 解奴辜、张貂

translations.literal: Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao
translations.idiomatic: Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao

sentences.zh: 解奴辜、张貂者，亦不知是何郡国人也。

translations.literal: As for Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao, likewise no one knew from what commandery or kingdom they were.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Nugu and Zhang Diao likewise left no record of their native place.

sentences.zh: 皆能隐沦，出入不由门户。

translations.literal: Both were able to conceal themselves and sink from sight, going in and out without using doors or gates.
translations.idiomatic: Both could melt from view and pass through walls without doors.

sentences.zh: 奴辜能变易物形，以诳幻人。

translations.literal: Nugu was able to change the forms of things in order to delude and dazzle people.
translations.idiomatic: Nugu could reshape objects to bewilder the eye.

sentences.zh: 又河南有□圣卿，善为丹书符劾，厌杀鬼神而使命之。

translations.literal: Also in Henan there was □ Shengqing, skilled at making cinnabar writings and talismanic binding, suppressing and killing ghosts and spirits and commanding them to run errands.
translations.idiomatic: Henan also had a certain Shengqing—one character of his name is lost in the text—who painted cinnabar talismans, smothered malignant spirits, and drafted them as servants.

sentences.zh: 又有编盲意，亦与鬼物交通。

translations.literal: There was also Bian Mangyi, who likewise had intercourse with ghostly things.
translations.idiomatic: Another wonder-worker, Bian Mangyi, trafficked with ghosts as well.

sentences.zh: 初，章帝时有寿光侯者，能劾百鬼众魅，令自缚见形。

translations.literal: In the beginning, under Emperor Zhang there was a man Marquis Shouguang who was able to impeach the hundred ghosts and the multitude of goblins, making them bind themselves and show their forms.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Zhang's reign Marquis Shouguang could arraign legions of sprites and force each to show its true body.

sentences.zh: 其乡人有妇为魅所病，侯为劾之，得大蛇数丈，死于门外。

translations.literal: A fellow villager had a woman afflicted by a goblin; the marquis impeached it for her and obtained a great snake several zhang long, dead outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor's wife fell under a demon, he bound the creature and produced a dead serpent many yards long outside her gate.

sentences.zh: 又有神树，人止者辄死，鸟过者必坠，侯复劾之，树盛夏枯落，见大蛇长七八丈，悬死其间。

translations.literal: There was also a divine tree: anyone who stopped there always died, and any bird that passed was sure to fall; the marquis again impeached it; in the height of summer the tree withered and dropped its leaves, and they saw a great snake seven or eight zhang long hanging dead within it.
translations.idiomatic: A "spirit tree" killed every traveler and dropped every bird that flew past; he exorcised it in midsummer until it shed its leaves, revealing a seven- or eight-yard serpent strangled in the crown.

sentences.zh: 帝闻而征之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him on report of these feats.

sentences.zh: 乃试问之：“吾殿下夜半后，常有数人，绛衣被发，持火相随，岂能劾之乎？

translations.literal: He then tried asking him, "Below my hall, after midnight, there are always several persons in crimson robes with loosened hair, carrying torches and following one another—can you impeach them?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tested him: "After midnight beneath my hall crimson phantoms with loose hair parade with torches—can you bind them?

sentences.zh: ”侯曰：“此小怪，易销耳。

translations.literal: " The marquis said, "These are small goblins; easy to dispose of.
translations.idiomatic: " Shouguang said, "Petty sprites—easily dismissed.

sentences.zh: ”帝伪使三人为之，侯劾三人，登时仆地无气。

translations.literal: " The emperor falsely had three men do it; the marquis impeached the three men, and immediately they collapsed to the ground without breath.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent three living attendants to fake the apparition; Shouguang's spell flattened all three, breathless.

sentences.zh: 帝大惊曰：“非魅也，朕相试耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly alarmed and said, "These are not goblins; I was testing you.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor cried, "Those were living men. I was only testing you."

sentences.zh: ”解之而苏。

translations.literal: " He released them and they revived.
translations.idiomatic: " He lifted the curse and they stirred awake.

sentences.zh: 甘始、东郭延年、封君达三人者，皆方士也。

translations.literal: Gan Shi, Dongguo Yannian, and Feng Junda—these three men were all recipe gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Shi, Dongguo Yannian, and Feng Junda were wandering adepts.

sentences.zh: 率能行容成御妇人术，或饮小便，或自倒悬，爱啬精气，不极视大言。

translations.literal: Generally they were able to practice Lord Rongcheng's method of controlling women in intercourse, or drink urine, or hang themselves upside down; they cherished and hoarded essential qi and did not exhaust themselves with staring or loud speech.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced Rongcheng's sexual yoga, drank their own urine, hung head-down, hoarded vital breath, and shunned strain and shouting.

sentences.zh: 甘始、元放、延年皆为操所录，问其术而行之。

translations.literal: Gan Shi, Zuo Ci styled Yuanfang, and Yannian were all taken into service by Cao Cao, who asked about their arts and practiced them.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao retained Gan Shi, Zuo Ci, and Yannian, questioned their regimens, and tried them himself.

sentences.zh: 君达号“青牛师”。

translations.literal: Junda was styled "Master of the Black Ox."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Junda was known as the Black Ox Master.

sentences.zh: 凡此数人，皆百余岁及二百岁也。

translations.literal: All these several persons lived beyond a hundred years and up to two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Each of them passed a century, some two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 王真、郝孟节

translations.literal: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie

sentences.zh: 王真、郝孟节者，皆上党人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie were both men of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen and Hao Mengjie came from Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 王真年且百岁，视之面有光泽，似未五十者。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen's years were nearly a hundred; looking at him, his face had luster, as though he were not yet fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen neared a hundred yet glowed like a man under fifty.

sentences.zh: 自云：“周流登五岳名山，悉能行胎息胎食之方，嗽舌下泉咽之，不绝房室。

translations.literal: He himself said, "I have roamed and ascended the five marchmounts and famous mountains, and in all cases am able to practice the methods of embryonic breathing and embryonic eating; I rinse the spring beneath the tongue and swallow it; I do not cut off intercourse with the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to have climbed the five sacred peaks, to swallow embryonic breath and embryonic essences, to press the saliva under his tongue and drink it down, and never to renounce sexual life.

sentences.zh: ”孟节能含枣核，不食可至五年十年。

translations.literal: " Mengjie was able to hold a jujube pit in his mouth and not eat yet reach five or ten years.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao Mengjie could hold a date stone under his tongue and fast five or ten years.

sentences.zh: 又能结气不息，身不动摇，状若死人，可至百日半年。

translations.literal: He was also able to knot his qi without ceasing, his body not swaying, appearing like a dead man, for up to a hundred days or half a year.
translations.idiomatic: He could seal his breath, lie motionless as a corpse, for half a year at a stretch.

sentences.zh: 亦有室家。

translations.literal: He also had wife and family.
translations.idiomatic: He still kept a household.

sentences.zh: 为人质谨不妄言，似士君子。

translations.literal: In personality he was plain and careful and did not speak rashly; he seemed a gentleman among scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Plain-spoken and cautious, he bore himself like a scholar.

sentences.zh: 曹操使领诸方士焉。

translations.literal: Cao Cao had him oversee the various recipe gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao put him in charge of the court's roster of adepts.

sentences.zh: 刘和平

translations.literal: Liu Heping
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heping

sentences.zh: 北海王和平，性好道术，自以当仙。

translations.literal: Wang Heping of Beihai by nature loved the arts of the Way and believed himself destined to become an immortal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Heping of Beihai loved Daoist arts and was sure he would transcend.

sentences.zh: 济南孙邕少事之，从至京师。

translations.literal: Sun Yong of Jinan in his youth served him and followed him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yong of Jinan studied under him in youth and followed him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 会和平病殁，邕因葬之东陶。

translations.literal: It happened that Heping died of illness; Yong therefore buried him at East Tao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang died of illness, Sun buried him at East Tao.

sentences.zh: 有书百余卷，药数囊，悉以送之。

translations.literal: There were more than a hundred scrolls of writings and several bags of drugs, all of which were sent down into the grave with him.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred fascicles of scripture and several sacks of elixirs went into the tomb with the corpse.

sentences.zh: 后弟子夏荣言其尸解，邕乃恨不取其宝书仙药焉。

translations.literal: Later his disciple Xia Rong said that he had undergone corpse liberation; Yong therefore regretted not having taken his precious books and immortal drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Later the disciple Xia Rong claimed Wang had "released the corpse"; Sun Yong rued the lost scriptures and elixirs he had left underground.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：幽贶罕征，明数难校。

translations.literal: The encomium states: Heaven's hidden boons are seldom proven manifest; luminous reckoning is hard to verify.
translations.idiomatic: Verdict: Heaven's covert signs rarely show themselves; reason cannot easily test them.

sentences.zh: 不探精远，歇感灵效？

translations.literal: If one does not investigate the recondite and remote, how can one exhaustively perceive spiritual efficacy?
translations.idiomatic: Without plumbing the farthest depths, who can fathom such powers?

sentences.zh: 如或迁讹，实乖玄奥。

translations.literal: If perchance there is shifting error, it truly contradicts the arcane subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Distorted tales only betray the mystery they claim to praise.
